title: GPU-SKU aware kernel registry + safe fallbacks + denylist plumbing for kernel auto-selection v2
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Introduce GPU-SKU keyed kernel mapping + explicit fallback hierarchy for kernel auto-selection v2, including denylist plumbing for known-bad kernel/SKU/driver combos. This is required to safely roll v2 to mixed fleets (A100/H100/L40S) without tail spikes from unstable kernels on specific SKUs.

Context
v1 effectively assumes “GPU class” and uses coarse capability checks. v2 selection logic introduces more kernel variants (prefill/decode, seq regimes), which makes SKU correctness + explicit fallbacks non-negotiable.

Scope
1) GPU SKU normalization
- Normalize device identity into a stable key used by the selector and telemetry.
- Support at minimum:
  - NVIDIA A100 (40GB / 80GB, PCIe vs SXM)
  - NVIDIA H100 (PCIe vs SXM)
  - NVIDIA L40S
- Treat MIG as a distinct “shape” and ensure we don’t accidentally apply full-GPU tuned kernels to MIG partitions.
- Explicitly include driver + CUDA runtime version as a gating feature for denylist evaluation (not as a primary selector dimension).

2) GPU-SKU keyed kernel registry
- Extend kernel registry mapping from {model_family, seq_bucket} -> kernel_set to {model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_key} -> kernel_set.
- Allow “wildcard” entries for GPU families to reduce duplication, with deterministic precedence rules (see Fallback Policy).

3) Safe fallback policy
- Implement explicit fallback hierarchy when:
  a) kernel not present for SKU
  b) kernel present but denied for SKU/driver/CUDA
  c) kernel present but marked unstable (runtime signal / config)
- Fallback order must be deterministic and observable.

4) Denylist plumbing
- Add denylist rules by (gpu_sku_key, kernel_id) with optional conditions:
  - driver_version range
  - cuda_version range
  - optional model_family scope (where needed)
- Denylist must be hot-reloadable via runtime config (through existing config loader plumbing) and safe under partial rollout.

Out of scope
- Learned scoring for selection (ADR decided rule-based).
- Adding new kernels themselves (owned by other tasks).

Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Selector receives a normalized gpu_sku_key and uses it in candidate lookup.
- [x] Kernel registry supports SKU-specific overrides and wildcard inheritance.
- [x] Fallback precedence is deterministic and unit-tested.
- [x] Denylist rules can disable (kernel_id, gpu_sku_key) with optional driver/CUDA guards.
- [x] Denylist is hot-reloadable without process restart.
- [x] Metrics/logs include gpu_sku_key and “denylist_hit=true/false” for sampled events.
- [x] A100/H100/L40S coverage in lightweight CI tests (mocked device IDs acceptable; perf validation handled in ENG-4825).

Implementation Notes
GPU SKU normalization proposal (initial)
- gpu_vendor: "nvidia"
- gpu_name: canonicalized name (e.g., "A100", "H100", "L40S")
- form_factor: "sxm" | "pcie" | "unknown"
- mem_gb: "40" | "80" | "48" | "unknown" (string, do not parse in critical path)
- mig: "true" | "false"
- sku_key format: "nvidia:<name>:<form_factor>:<mem_gb>:mig=<true|false>"

Fallback policy (deterministic)
Given (model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_key):
1) Exact match: (family, bucket, exact sku_key)
2) SKU wildcard: (family, bucket, "<name>:*" equivalent)
3) Family wildcard: (family, "*", sku_key)
4) Global default: ("*", "*", "*")
At each level: filter out denied kernels (denylist), then select best remaining candidate per v2 rules.
If no candidates remain: fall back to v1 kernel selection path (explicit metric emitted).

Denylist rule format (runtime config)
- rule_id
- match:
  - gpu_sku_key (exact or prefix match)
  - kernel_id
  - optional driver_version_min/max
  - optional cuda_version_min/max
- action: deny

Rollout Plan
- Land behind v2 feature gate (selector still defaults to v1 unless v2 enabled).
- Add initial denylist entries for known unstable combos from early canary (see Known Issues doc once created).
- Validate on perf-canary scenarios before enabling v2 in Hosted canary region.

Test Plan
- Unit tests:
  - normalization: device name variants, MIG detection paths
  - registry lookup precedence
  - denylist evaluation with driver/CUDA boundaries
  - determinism: identical inputs => identical chosen kernel_id
- Integration tests:
  - config hot reload toggles denylist and affects selection within N seconds
  - fallback to v1 when all candidates denied

Risks / Edge cases
- Cloud SKU naming inconsistencies (e.g., instance types vs CUDA device name). Prefer CUDA device properties; fall back to a conservative “unknown” and disable SKU-specialized kernels.
- Metric cardinality increase from sku_key; keep sku_key to a bounded set and ensure normalization doesn’t leak vendor strings/driver build metadata.
